title: The legacy criterion of RWB-E4-043 names no settlement, its test cases carry no settlement data, and the story master gives no requirement id
source: Legacy RWB-E4-043 (Story, Acceptance criteria, Data, Test cases); FSD P8 Payments and posting v3 A2.3.4.1 (AC-P8-003-01); work package line for RWB-P8-E4043-APP (reqs empty)
description: The story owns two legacy criteria word for word and both are generic. AC1 reads 'Given the data and the rule version this feature needs are in place / When its trigger arrives / Then matches a settlement payment to the treatment and closes the money side' and AC2 reads 'Given the decision log cannot be written / When the action is taken / Then nothing changes and the user sees MSG-P7-003'. The four legacy test cases repeat the same rows with no settlement-specific value: no case, no treatment, no receipt, no amount and no business date. The FSD keeps the feature as FEAT-PAY-03 and its main success criterion AC-P8-003-01 is one line marked 'Written one epic ahead', so the module document adds no value either. The split plan carries no requirement id for this slice, which is why section 18 traces the two criteria to FEAT-PAY-03 and AC-P8-003-01 rather than to a requirement row. The story therefore keeps the two criteria unchanged and supplies its own synthetic settlement data set, which is where the settlement detail comes from.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-043 AC1 and AC2 as quoted; legacy test cases TC-E4-043-01 'Match a settlement payment' and TC-E4-043-02 'Not recorded' with no data column; FSD P8 v3 A2.3.4.1 AC-P8-003-01 'The data and rules it needs are in place / The trigger arrives / The result is recorded with its rule version / Written one epic ahead'; the FSD 'Requirements served' table of P8 is empty.
owner_role: P8 business analyst and the FSD owner
proposed: Have the Settlement route set owner confirm the settlement data set the E4 build tests on (case, settlement treatment, receipt of source CUSTOMER on the business date, amount matched to SETTLEMENT) and carry it into the Story test cases tab of the Test Cases master under the same four test case IDs; add the requirement row of FEAT-PAY-03 to the Requirements served table of FSD P8 in its next version.

title: The settlement match has no published package code, rule IDs, tolerance, window or outcome fields, and the consumed reads have no published operation names
source: Legacy RWB-E4-043 (Story, Data, Endpoints); FSD P8 v3 A2.3.2 and A2.3.4.4; TSD P8 v2 T3.1 (payment_match_rule, DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273), T-A.1 and T-A.2; context pack P8 ownership rows; Template and Rules R4 and R7.3
description: The story must state what fires the settlement arm, what the arm evaluates, what it answers and what it reads on the other services' contracts. No source gives the package code or the rule IDs of the settlement match: the FSD describes the step as 'receives its trigger: a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer' and the TSD names the matching rule table payment_match_rule with amount_tolerance_pct, window_days_before, window_days_after, grace_days and partial_floor_pct as columns, but every one of those rows is data and no value is published for the settlement arm. No source publishes the operation names of the three consumed reads either: the payment facts of the ACE batch (P1), the case reference and the money-side answer (P3) and the package read (P7); the treatment read is the only named one, GET /treatments/{treatmentId} of rwb-treatment. The outcome fields and the case move that follow the money-side close are rwb-case's and are not named. The story builds the step, holds every one of those values as a rule row, reference data or a placeholder, and names no invented rule, threshold or operation.
evidence: FSD P8 v3 A2.3.2 step 1 reads 'Receives its trigger: a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer'; TSD P8 v2 T3.1 lists payment_match_rule with DF-REF-264 amount_tolerance_pct, DF-REF-266 window_days_before, DF-REF-267 window_days_after, DF-REF-268 grace_days and DF-REF-269 partial_floor_pct but publishes no row value; TSD P8 v2 T-A.1 lists only API-P8-001 and API-P8-002, both provided; the context pack lists the two P8 provided operations and no consumed one.
owner_role: P7 rule owner and the P8 solution architect
proposed: Publish the settlement arm of the PAYMENT_MATCH package with its package code, rule IDs, tolerance, window and grace in the rule registry, name the three consumed operations in the API Specification and the Service Contract Catalog, and let rwb-case publish the money-side answer and the outcome code; the story then replaces the placeholder with the published values and changes no criterion.

title: The legacy story reads v_ace_payment and v_ace_batch_status in process while the target gives the ACE views to rwb-source-data alone
source: Legacy RWB-E4-043 (Data, Endpoints); FSD P8 v3 change note and A2.3.3.1 (VR-P8-003-1); context pack P8 (no ACE grant) and the slide 8 note on the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-05
description: The legacy Data table lists v_ace_payment with DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054 as a source of the match and VR-P8-003-1 reads v_ace_batch_status for the staleness check, both in process. In the target only rwb-source-data holds SELECT on the recovery.v_ace_* views, and every other service holds no grant, so DP-05 applies to this service as a prohibition and not as a permission: the receipt facts and the batch status arrive on the rwb-source-data contract. The story keeps the staleness rule and its message exactly and moves the read, and the difference between the legacy data table and the target grant is recorded here so that the FSD data table and the DP-05 row agree in their next versions.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-043 Data row 'v_ace_payment | payment_code, account_key, payment_date, payment_amount, payment_channel, capital_amount and 6 more | DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054'; FSD P8 v3 A2.3.3.1 VR-P8-003-1 reads v_ace_batch_status; the context pack describes the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views as read only by rwb-source-data and lists no ACE table among the P8 ownership rows.
owner_role: P1 source-data owner and the P8 solution architect
proposed: Keep the receipt read and the batch-status check on the rwb-source-data contract with its freshness stamp, retire the v_ace_payment and v_ace_batch_status reads of this service, and correct the Data table of FSD P8 and the DP-05 row of the pattern table so that no service but rwb-source-data is drawn as an ACE view reader.

title: The work package gives the contract-dependency row as None while the story consumes four contracts, and it still starts on Day 1
source: Work package line for RWB-P8-E4043-APP (C empty, Ready to start Day 1, lane L-P8-F); the consumed rows of section 12.2; Template and Rules R5.4 and R5.7
description: The metadata row 'Contract dependencies' is None because the work package gives C as an empty array, but the step cannot run without four reads: the receipt of the ACE batch (P1), the case reference and the money-side answer (P3), the settlement treatment (S2) and the package in force (P7). Under R5.4 a class C row never blocks the build, so the two statements do not contradict each other in effect, but they do in the plan: the four rows are built against their published documents and fakes from Day 1 and the plan's C row records none of them. The story keeps the metadata row exactly as the work package gives it and records the four reads in 12.2, 12.8 and 13.
evidence: The work package line gives 'C': [] and 'Ready to start': 'Day 1' for lane L-P8-F; section 12.2 of the story lists GET /treatments/{treatmentId} and three reads whose operation names are not published; Template and Rules R5.4 reads 'C | Another service's CON story. Build against the published contract and its fake. | No'.
owner_role: P8 solution architect and the split-plan owner
proposed: Add the four consumed rows to the C list of this slice in the next split-plan version (RWB-P1 source-data, RWB-P3 case, RWB-S2 treatment, RWB-P7 decision contract stories) and keep the Day-1 rule of R5.7 unchanged; the story needs no change because it already builds against the documents and fakes.

title: TSD P8 names MatchRequest and ProceedsPage without a field list, so the request and the page have to be derived
source: TSD P8 v2 T-A.1 and T-A.2 (API-P8-001, API-P8-002); TSD P8 v2 T3.1 and T3.2; legacy RWB-E4-043 (Endpoints)
description: The contract baseline must publish the request body of the match and the page element of the proceeds list. The TSD gives the operation purposes, the query parameters matched, from, to, page and size, the answers ProceedsPage and Proceeds, and the error sets, and it gives the nine columns of proceeds and the two lists, but it gives no field list for MatchRequest and no page envelope beyond the four query parameters. The baseline derives the request from the nine columns and the match the app story describes, derives the page from the pagination convention of the platform, marks every derived field with the placeholder, and adds no business value.
evidence: TSD P8 v2 T-A.2 API-P8-002 reads 'Request | MatchRequest' and API-P8-001 reads 'Response | ProceedsPage' with no element tables; TSD P8 v2 T3.1 gives DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009 with no request or page definition.
owner_role: P8 solution architect and the API specification owner
proposed: Publish the MatchRequest element as the case reference, the treatment reference, the account payment reference, the amount, the received date and the match value, and the ProceedsPage element as the page of Proceeds with page, size and total, in the next version of TSD P8 appendix T-A and in the API Specification file of rwb-payment.

title: The payloads of TreatmentBooked and ProceedsMatched are not published, while PaymentMissed is
source: Architecture v5 slides 42 and 43 (EV-11, EV-12, EV-25); TSD P8 v2 T5.3; context pack P8 events (EV-11, EV-12, EV-25); Template and Rules R4
description: This service owns three events and the contract baseline publishes one schema for each. Only PaymentMissed carries a published example (caseId, treatmentId, dueDate, amountDue, daysLate). TreatmentBooked and ProceedsMatched are named, with their producers and consumers, but no source gives their payload: the TSD lists the three names as published and gives no field, and the event catalogue is not yet written. The baseline writes the two schemas from the CloudEvents envelope, the modelled columns of proceeds and treatment and the match value, marks every field that no source gives with the placeholder, and registers them in BACKWARD mode so that the owner can settle the field list without a breaking change.
evidence: TSD P8 v2 T5.3 lists TreatmentBooked, PaymentMissed and ProceedsMatched as Published with no payload; the context pack lists EV-11, EV-12 and EV-25 for P8 with no field list; the PaymentMissed example carries caseId, treatmentId, dueDate, amountDue and daysLate.
owner_role: P8 solution architect and the event catalogue owner
proposed: Publish the field list of rwb.payment.TreatmentBooked.v1 and rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1 in the Kafka Topic and Event Catalog v1 and in the AsyncAPI document of rwb-payment, keyed by case id with identifiers, amounts, dates, list values and a rule version only, and keep the registry in BACKWARD mode.

title: The settlement money side is rule R-SET-14, but the matching mechanism has no package code and no rule IDs, and payment_match_rule is replaced
source: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-SET-13, R-SET-14, R-SET-21, R-SET-23, R-SET-24); TSD P8 v2 T3.1 (payment_match_rule, DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273); Temporal and Drools design (PAYMENT_MATCH replaces payment_match_rule); context pack P8 ownership rows (one table, proceeds)
description: R-SET-14 is the row that matches a settlement payment and posts it (AWAITING_PAYMENT to PAYMENT_CLEARED, amount_received = settlement_amount), so the money side of this feature has a named rule. What has no source is the mechanism around it: the package code of the matching rule set, the rule IDs of the tolerance, window and partial rows, and their values. The TSD models payment_match_rule as a table of this module, while the target carries one table in rwb_payment (proceeds) and the Temporal and Drools design replaces that table with the PAYMENT_MATCH package governed in rwb-decision, so the rows are not this service's to own or to migrate. The contract names R-SET-14 and the PAYMENT_MATCH package, fixes no package code and no rule ID, and carries the placeholder.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-SET-14 'AWAITING_PAYMENT | PAYMENT_RECEIVED | amount_received = settlement_amount | Match the payment and post it | PAYMENT_CLEARED'; TSD P8 v2 T3.1 payment_match_rule DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273; the context pack lists one P8 table, proceeds, and no payment_match_rule.
owner_role: P7 rule owner and the P8 solution architect
proposed: Record in the rule registry that R-SET-14 is the settlement money-side transition, publish the PAYMENT_MATCH package code and the IDs of its tolerance, window and partial rows with their values, and retire payment_match_rule from the TSD data model in favour of the package.
